reading.rtitle: Specification SP-207 -- everything is approved, and nobody can give a date
paras: This memo is one page long because the project only has one real problem, and it is at the bottom. The specification for the new reference has already been approved, in version four, by quality and by the plant. Nine requirements are listed, and all nine are mandatory: there is nothing on that list that anybody can decide to skip in order to gain two weeks. The prototype has just arrived from the lab, two kilos of it, and it does exactly what the document says it should do.

So far, every line is green. Then comes the line that decides everything. The product requires a shelf life of twelve months, and the shelf life test has not started yet. That test takes twelve weeks, and there is no version of it that takes less. You cannot buy speed, you cannot add people to it, and you cannot start it before there is something to put on the shelf. Twelve weeks from the day it starts is the earliest possible answer, and the answer might still be no.

There is a second line, and it is written as a note from the plant at the bottom of the approval. The plant has signed the specification, and the plant has also written that this specification describes a two-kilo batch, while the line produces two tons. Those are not the same product in any way that matters to a factory. The time the mixture needs changes. The temperature in the middle of the batch changes. A machine that cannot stop behaves differently from a laboratory that can. The trial run in the real line has not been scheduled yet.

The memo therefore asks the commercial team for exactly one thing, and it is not patience. It is silence about dates. Nobody has promised a launch to any customer, and nobody should, until the shelf life result exists and the trial run has been made. Both of those have a cost measured in weeks, and both of them are cheaper than one date given to a buyer and missed.

choices: It is blocked by a document that nobody has approved
Everything is approved, but two tests have not been done, and until they are, no date can be given
It is finished and only waiting for the commercial team to launch it

listenings.text: I will give you the whole picture in two minutes, and then you can ask me anything. What is done. The specification has been approved, version four, by quality and by the plant, both signatures. The prototype has just arrived, two kilos, and it behaves exactly the way the document says it should. So the product, as an idea, works. Now the part that is not done, and there is only one that matters. We have not started the shelf life test. Twelve weeks, and before anybody asks: no, it cannot be made faster, no, we cannot run it in parallel with something else, and no, more people do not help. It is time in a warehouse. That is the whole test. So here is what I need from this room, and it is not patience, it is silence. Please do not give a launch date to any customer before that result is in. If we promise a date and the answer comes back negative, we do not lose twelve weeks. We lose the customer.

Every product that comes down to me arrives with a beautiful document written for two kilos, and then I am asked to make two tons of it. And people look at me as if that were the same thing with a bigger number in front. It is not. When the quantity changes, the time the mixture needs changes, because the middle of a two-ton batch does not behave like the middle of a bowl. The temperature changes for the same reason. And my line cannot stop. A laboratory can stop, look at something, think about it and start again. A production line that stops is a production line that has thrown away everything inside it. So what I ask for is always the same, and I have been asking for eleven years. One trial run in the real line before the specification is closed. One. It costs a day and a half and some material, and it saves three months of arguing about whose fault it is, which is a thing I have also done for eleven years and enjoy considerably less.
